lede: A flow in the latent code reconstructs softly, clearer than RealNVP and close to an ordinary VAE.
points: Normalizing flow in the latent space
title: f-VAE
question: Does a RealNVP inside the VAE latent space improve reconstruction and likelihood on digits?
process: This model is a VAE with a RealNVP flow on the latent sample, before the decoder. Each coupling keeps one part of the vector and scales and shifts the rest. The log-determinant adds the scale only on the coordinates that change.
The KL term is the change-of-variables divergence of that transformed sample from the unit normal. There is one Monte Carlo estimate per image:
The loss has the same shape as the ordinary VAE loss. Squared error is summed over pixels, β multiplies the KL after the flow, and both terms are averaged over the batch.
Samples in the gallery do not invert the flow. They draw z from N(0, I) and decode it. The flow sits inside the posterior, not on the path from the prior to the image.

Both runs use the full training split, latent size 32, and four couplings. On digits, test MSE is 0.0554, ELBO is −69.35, and the log-determinant is −12.87. On Fashion-MNIST, test MSE is 0.0621, ELBO is −65.00, and the log-determinant is −9.07.

opening.summary: Training and test agree on both full splits. Each row gives the reconstruction, the ELBO, or the comparison with RealNVP and the ordinary VAE.
opening.hover: Each row is one part of the test record.

marks.label: Reconstruction
marks.summary: Test MSE is 0.0554 and MAE is 0.0920. The training figures are 0.0555 and 0.0923. The flowed posterior mean keeps the digit and softens the stroke. This is a full run of 60,000 images at latent size 32, so it is not the same setup as the latent-8 slice used for the ordinary VAE.

marks.label: Likelihood
marks.summary: Test ELBO is −69.35 and bits per dimension are 0.953, against a training ELBO of −69.40 and the same 0.953 bits per dimension. The bound held on the 10,000 test images. A Gaussian decoder can report a decent bits-per-dimension figure while the pictures stay soft, because the likelihood averages over where the stroke sits.
marks.hover: Test ELBO −69.35. Test bits per dimension 0.953.

marks.label: Flow
marks.summary: The test log-determinant is −12.87 and the training value is −12.85. The flow is not an identity at the end of training: it rescales volume in the latent space. The KL stays near 19.5 on both splits. A gallery image is still a decode of N(0, I). The inverse flow is used in the posterior, not as the generator for the gallery.

marks.label: Prior samples
marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: The 64 digit samples cover 0 through 9, plus a few ambiguous blobs. They are cleaner than the RealNVP inverse grid, which is mostly stroke fragments. They are softer than a sharp GAN, and they sit in the same family as the ordinary VAE samples. That ordinary digit VAE is a 10,000-image slice at latent size 8, with test MSE 0.0852. This run is the full split at latent size 32, with test MSE 0.0554, so the lower error is a larger experiment, not a paired win. The gallery decodes N(0, I). The inverse flow stays inside the posterior.
marks.frameCaption: f-VAE digits drawn from N(0, I).

marks.label: Fashion-MNIST
marks.summary: Same hyperparameters, 20 epochs, and the full split. Test ELBO is −65.00 and bits per dimension are 0.945, against a training ELBO of −64.33. Test MSE is 0.0621 and MAE is 0.1328. The KL is 12.95 and the log-determinant is −9.07. Samples from the prior read as shirts, trousers, dresses, shoes, and bags, which is clearer than the RealNVP Fashion-MNIST blobs. The ordinary Fashion-MNIST VAE, at latent size 8 on a slice, has test MSE 0.0749 and ELBO −71.09. The shirt logo and the thin sandal still disappear, the same failure as that VAE.
marks.frameCaption: f-VAE Fashion-MNIST drawn from N(0, I). Garments, without print or straps.

reflection.worked: Training and test agree on both full splits. The log-determinant is −12.87 on digits and −9.07 on Fashion-MNIST, and the sample grids cover many classes. Those grids are clearer than the RealNVP inverses.
reflection.unexpected: Fashion-MNIST’s better ELBO (−65.00 against −69.35) comes with a worse pixel error (MSE 0.0621 against 0.0554). The shirt print is gone, and the Fashion-MNIST loss is still falling at epoch 20. The pictures stay in the same soft family as the ordinary VAE.
reflection.why: Samples decode N(0, I) and do not invert the flow. Bits per dimension near 0.95 are the ELBO of a Gaussian decoder, a different number from the RealNVP value of 3.263. A reasonable reading is that squared error averages away a logo and a sandal strap, because many textures share one code.
reflection.improve: Train Fashion-MNIST past epoch 20. Match the ordinary VAE’s split and latent size before calling this a win. A sharper print needs a different decoder likelihood. More couplings will not, by themselves, sharpen a Gaussian decoder.
